subject: Medicine
concept: Major parasitic diseases in the Hematology Medicine block can produce fever, anemia, splenomegaly or lymphatic disease.

content.definition: Major parasitic diseases in the Hematology Medicine block can produce fever, anemia, splenomegaly or lymphatic disease.
content.explanation: Malaria can cause hemolysis, anemia and thrombocytopenia; visceral leishmaniasis can cause prolonged fever, splenomegaly and pancytopenia; lymphatic filariasis causes lymphatic obstruction and chronic lymphedema.
content.mechanism: Malaria can cause hemolysis, anemia and thrombocytopenia; visceral leishmaniasis can cause prolonged fever, splenomegaly and pancytopenia; lymphatic filariasis causes lymphatic obstruction and chronic lymphedema.
content.clinical_relevance: Malaria may cause hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia. Severe malaria requires prompt treatment. Visceral leishmaniasis can present with fever, splenomegaly and cytopenias. Filariasis causes chronic lymphatic disease.
content.diagnosis: Diagnosis uses the appropriate clinical, laboratory, microbiologic, marrow or blood-bank studies for the suspected condition.
content.treatment: Management is disease- and patient-specific and should follow current authoritative guidance.
